train noun

also compartment, train compartment, passenger train

modern

M-O s.v. train
Traupman 211, 219, 397

trāmen, trāminis n.

noun, third declension

Train in modern Latin. Morgan–Owens traces the lexical form trāmen to Charisius; the railway sense is modern. Related vocabulary: trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — draw or pull.

Other words

  • trāmen ferriviārium — railway train

    also used · modern

  • hamaxostichus, hamaxostichī m.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern

    A competing learned Neo-Latin term for a train.

  • trāmen commūne — passenger train

    also used · modern · Traupman 357

Examples

  • Trāmine īmus.

    We’re going by train.composed

  • Trāmen advenit.

    The train is arriving.composed

  • Quotā hōrā trāmen meum abscēdit?

    At what time does my train leave?Traupman 211

  • Ā quotā crepīdine trāmen abscēdit?

    From which platform does the train leave?Traupman 211

  • diaeta (prīmae, secundae classis)

    a (first-class, second-class) compartmentTraupman 294

See also railway, train station, tram.
